skill.name: container-orchestration
skill.description: Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, Docker Compose, and AWS ECS/Fargate guidance for building, deploying, and operating containerized applications.
skill.summary: Create and review container orchestration patterns for Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, Docker Compose, and AWS ECS/Fargate.
skill.author: 0xDarkMatter

security_audit.summary: I confirmed risks where templates or examples include weak default credentials, plaintext secret values, an executable Bash build script, and a debugpy listener on all interfaces. Most static hits are false positives from fenced examples, normal Docker cache cleanup, localhost health checks, Kubernetes references, and safe documentation links. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Weak default database credentials in Compose templates
remediation.suggestion: Remove postgres fallback passwords and require users to provide DB_PASSWORD through a local env file or secret manager.

remediation.issue: Plaintext secret values in Kubernetes and Compose examples
remediation.suggestion: Replace user:pass and supersecretkey with non-secret placeholders and prefer ExternalSecret or secret manager examples.

remediation.issue: Debugpy listens on all interfaces in the debug Dockerfile example
remediation.suggestion: Bind debugpy to 127.0.0.1 or document strict local-only port forwarding and network isolation requirements.

remediation.issue: Build script can build and optionally push container images
remediation.suggestion: Add a dry-run mode, confirm registry pushes, and validate registry, tag, Dockerfile, and context arguments before execution.

content.user_title: Deploy Containers with Docker, Kubernetes, and ECS
content.value_statement: Container deployment patterns are easy to misconfigure across Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, and ECS. This skill provides templates, examples, and references for safer container orchestration workflows.
actual_capabilities: Provides Dockerfile patterns for multi-stage builds, non-root users, health checks, caching, and debug targets.
Includes a Docker Compose starter template with app, database, Redis, health checks, volumes, and network configuration.
Documents Kubernetes manifests for Namespace, ConfigMap, Secret, Deployment, Service, Ingress, HPA, PDB, RBAC, NetworkPolicy, and CronJob.
Shows Helm chart structure, values files, helper templates, deployment templates, and common Helm commands.
Explains AWS ECS on Fargate architecture, networking, IAM roles, secrets, scaling, observability, deployment options, and failure modes.
Includes a Bash helper script for building Docker images and optionally pushing them to a registry.
limitations: Examples require review and customization before production use.
The skill does not inspect live clusters unless the user provides context or asks to run commands.
The build script assumes Docker, Git, and registry credentials are already configured.
Cloud provider details can change, so AWS and Kubernetes versions should be verified against official documentation.

use_cases.title: Create a container deployment baseline
use_cases.description: Use the Dockerfile and Compose templates to start a service with health checks, non-root execution, and local dependencies.

use_cases.title: Review Kubernetes production manifests
use_cases.description: Compare deployments, services, ingress, RBAC, scaling, disruption budgets, and network policies against documented patterns.

use_cases.title: Choose between ECS Fargate and Kubernetes
use_cases.description: Use the Fargate reference to evaluate operations burden, AWS integration, networking, IAM, scaling, and deployment tooling.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Dockerfile
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production Dockerfile for my application. Include a non-root user, dependency caching, a health check, and clear notes for values I must customize.

prompt_templates.title: Build Local Compose Stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a Docker Compose setup for an app with Postgres and Redis. Use safe placeholders, explain required environment variables, and include health checks.

prompt_templates.title: Review Kubernetes Manifests
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these Kubernetes manifests for reliability and security. Check probes, resources, secret handling, RBAC, network policy, autoscaling, and rollout behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Design ECS Fargate Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an ECS Fargate deployment for this service. Cover task definition, networking, IAM roles, secrets, scaling, logging, load balancing, and failure modes.

output_examples.input: Review my Dockerfile for production readiness.
output: Identifies missing non-root execution, weak dependency caching, missing health checks, and unnecessary runtime packages.
Recommends a multi-stage build, pinned base image, smaller runtime image, and clear runtime environment variables.

output_examples.input: Help me prepare Kubernetes manifests for a web service.
output: Produces a deployment checklist covering probes, resource requests, secret references, pod security context, service exposure, and rollout safety.
Highlights where placeholders must be replaced before applying manifests to a cluster.

output_examples.input: Should this workload use ECS Fargate or Kubernetes?
output: Compares operational complexity, AWS integration, portability, scheduling needs, cost levers, and team experience.
Recommends a deployment path and lists the main risks to validate before implementation.

best_practices: Review every template value before production use, especially credentials, image names, exposed ports, and resource limits.
Use secret managers or Kubernetes Secret references instead of committing real secret values into examples or manifests.
Test health checks, probes, rollout behavior, and rollback paths before promoting container changes.
anti_patterns: Do not copy placeholder credentials or default passwords into shared environments.
Do not expose debug listeners or admin ports on public interfaces.
Do not run build or push scripts without confirming the target registry, tag, Dockerfile, and build context.

faq.question: Does this skill create production-ready manifests automatically?
faq.answer: It provides strong starting patterns, but users must customize and review every value before production use.

faq.question: Can it help with both Docker and Kubernetes?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Dockerfiles, Docker Compose, Kubernetes manifests, Helm charts, and ECS Fargate guidance.

faq.question: Does it require live cluster access?
faq.answer: No. It can work from files and user-provided context, but live checks require explicit user permission and tooling.

faq.question: Does it manage secrets safely by default?
faq.answer: It includes secret-handling patterns, but some examples need safer placeholders before publication or production reuse.

faq.question: Can it build and push images?
faq.answer: The package includes a Bash helper script for Docker builds and optional pushes, which users should inspect before running.

faq.question: Is ECS Fargate covered separately from Kubernetes?
faq.answer: Yes. The Fargate reference covers AWS-native networking, IAM roles, secrets, scaling, logging, deployment tools, and common failures.
